content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement. To the contrary, § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer has given no such commitment.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding Customer. Searches for "solicit", "recruit", "induce", "hire", and "employ" across the full document, plus review of the likely homes for such a covenant (§ 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General), returned no restrictive covenant on hiring. This matches the preferred position: no non-solicit on Customer. Section 12.3 goes further in our favour by expressly reserving Customer's freedom to hire any person responding to general recruitment and recording that Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment", so the fallback's scope, duration, and general-advertising carve-out are not engaged. Note that § 12.4 imposes a narrow non-compete on Vendor only; that burdens the counterparty and benefits us, so it is not flagged. No redline required.
